summary.text: Julia Salazar is the incumbent Democratic and Working Families Party state senator for District 18 in Brooklyn and Queens, first elected in 2018 as a former community organizer. She chairs the Senate's Crime Victims, Crime and Correction Committee and, according to her campaign website, serves as Deputy Majority Leader for Senate and Assembly Relations. She is unopposed in the general election.

paragraphs.text: Attended Columbia University, where, per her official Senate biography, her advocacy began on tenant and worker issues; Wikipedia reports she did not earn a degree there.
Worked as a community organizer with Jews for Racial & Economic Justice (JFREJ), focusing on criminal justice and police accountability, before her 2018 election.

In 2018, as a first-time candidate, defeated incumbent Martin Malave Dilan in the Democratic primary for State Senate District 18 and was elected, taking office in January 2019; per her official Senate biography, she was the youngest woman elected in the history of the New York State Senate.
Chairs the Senate Crime Victims, Crime and Correction Committee; previously chaired the Senate Committee on Women's Issues.
According to her campaign website, serves as Deputy Majority Leader for Senate and Assembly Relations and as Treasurer of the legislature's Black, Puerto Rican, Hispanic & Asian Caucus.

Her official biography says her first bill to pass was the Comprehensive Contraception Coverage Act and that she played a key role in the 2019 Housing Stability and Tenant Protection Act and led the 2021 HALT Solitary Confinement Act.
District 18 includes Bushwick, Cypress Hills-East New York and parts of Williamsburg in Brooklyn and parts of Ridgewood, Queens.
